newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher after February CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher after February CPI.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Sunday in dull trading following the release of the February consumer price index (CPI) on Friday, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.01 pct to 103.73
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct at 103.03
Volume was a very low 94 million shekels.

"Most of the activity was concentrated in CPI-linked short bonds. The CPI was relatively high and institutional investors want to protect themselves against rising inflation," said Yossi Wiedelfeld of Eyal Securities.
The February CPI, released on Friday, rose 1.2 percent compared with a 0.4 percent increase in January. The CPI was was at the top of economists' forecasts.

"Inflation-linked bonds are expected to continue rising in the near future. The government stopped issuing these bonds and there is a real shortage in the market," said Zvi Hoffman of Meitav Investments and Securities.
Traders said activity in unlinked bonds was mixed and volume low.
"The Bank of Israel is expected to leave its key lending rate unchanged. I think unlinked bonds will continue rising with yields falling further," Hoffman said.
"The rise of the Makam was nothing special and they usually rise after the weekend," Wedelfeld said.
Dollar-linked bonds closed higher in thin trading after the shekel weakened against the dollar on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
